Radio and CAT
Control your connected radio. You only see what your radio supports; the rest is listed under “Not available”.
Satellites

Digital modes
FT8, APRS, SSTV and Morse. Transmitting goes on the air: check your licence, frequency and power.
Channels and templates
Edit channels or build regional lists. Always make a backup before writing to the radio.
Logbook
Your contacts, stored on the phone. No network and no radio needed.
Tools
Checks and aids to get the connection to your radio working.
Export or import all your data as JSON. The file contains positions and contacts: share it only with people who should have it.
Version, scope of the app and privacy. No data is collected or sent.
Your profile stores radio, connection and callsign once. The home screen adapts to it.
Set up your radio once in the profile and this screen only shows the actions that radio supports. Tap “?” on any section for its help.
Not available with %1$s (%2$d)

Connection not tested

Set up your radio
Choose your radio once and the app will show only what it can do. Tap “Set up profile” to start.
Set up profile
Callsign: %1$s
Locator: %1$s
Multi-radio CAT
Frequency, mode, meters and memories of your radio.
Control frequency, mode and memories over USB and track satellites with Doppler. You need the data cable and a configured profile. Check antenna and power before transmitting.
Quansheng UV-K5 CAT
Tune and listen with your UV-K5 over USB (receive only).
Connect the UV-K5 over USB and tune a receive frequency. You need the data cable and compatible firmware. This is an experimental feature and does not transmit.
RT-950 Pro over Bluetooth
Backup, APRS, messages and zones.
Connect over Bluetooth LE with the RT-950 Pro switched on and nearby. Always make a backup before writing to the radio.
APRS chat
APRS messages through a KISS TNC.
Uses the callsign from your profile as the source. You need a KISS link over Bluetooth or network. Sending is transmitting: check frequency and licence.
USB diagnostics
Check cables, ports and the radio’s response.
Lists USB devices and tests communication with your radio. Use it when the connection fails. It does not transmit.
OpenGD77
Screen and clock of your radio over USB.
Connect the radio running OpenGD77 firmware over USB to see its screen and set the clock. It does not transmit.
Quansheng channels
Edit, back up and restore UV-K5 channels (Beta).
Reads and writes channels over USB. Make a full backup first: writing replaces the radio’s channels. Beta feature.
Channel templates
Regional lists ready to export (RX only).
Builds offline templates for your radio; nothing needs to be connected. Check local regulations before transmitting.
SSTV from WAV
Decode Robot36 images from a WAV file.
Pick a recorded WAV and get the picture. Works with any radio, or without one, and does not transmit.
Live Morse and Robot36
Receive with the phone microphone and decode.
Hold the radio speaker near the phone microphone and grant the permission when asked. Receive only.
AZ/EL rotor
Point your antenna with the BricoHams rotor.
Connects over Bluetooth to the BricoHams rotor. Make sure the area is clear before moving the antenna.
Satellites
Passes, map and Doppler, offline.
Computes passes from saved TLEs and your profile position. No radio needed; with CAT it can correct Doppler.
FT8 and digital modes
Decode and transmit FT8/FT4.
You need the radio connected, the phone clock accurate and your callsign in the profile. Transmitting goes on the air: check power and licence.
Logbook
Log contacts; import and export ADIF.
Stores your contacts on the phone with duplicate detection and ADIF/JSON export. Works offline.
Connection
Operator
Summary
Four steps, just once: choose your radio, test the connection, enter your callsign and location, and review the summary. You can edit it any time.
Choose the radio you use. The home screen will show only what it can do.
Say how the radio connects and tap “Test connection”. Testing does not transmit.
Your callsign is used in the logbook, APRS, FT8 and SSTV. The location is optional and serves satellites and the locator.
Review the data and the tools that will be active. Tap “Save profile” to finish.
Supports: %1$s
USB serial: the radio connects through a USB-serial cable or adapter (FTDI, CP210x, CH340 chips). This is the usual choice for Yaesu, Icom and (tr)uSDX.
USB CDC: the radio shows up directly as a USB port, with no adapter chip (QMX, QDX, OpenGD77). A USB OTG cable is enough.
Bluetooth LE: no cable. The radio is searched for and paired from its own screen.
Network (TCP): an external KISS TNC reached over Wi-Fi.
Connect the radio over USB with an OTG cable, switch it on and tap “Test connection”.

Tools enabled with this radio
All set. Tap “Save profile” to finish.
Choose the model and speed, then connect over USB. You need the data cable and the radio switched on. Connecting does not transmit.
Read and change frequency and mode (VFO A/B). Changing frequency does not transmit.
Shows S-meter, power and SWR when the radio sends them. Read only.
Prepare and send FT8/FT4 and other digital modes over CAT. Transmitting goes on the air: check antenna, power and licence.
Read, edit and save the radio’s memories. Make a backup before writing.
Automatic Doppler: VFO A for downlink and VFO B for uplink with split. Needs your profile position and TLEs; if you transmit, watch your power.
Send SSTV images through the radio. This is a transmission: check frequency, mode and licence; you can stop it at any time.
Search for the radio over Bluetooth LE and connect. Switch it on and keep it close. Connecting does not transmit.
Save and restore a copy of the radio. Make a backup before any write.
Set up APRS with your profile callsign. Sending beacons is transmitting: check frequency and licence.
Read and send APRS messages. Sending goes on the air.
Prepare satellite channels in the radio. You need your position in the profile. Writing changes memories: make a backup first.
Plan and write channel zones. Writing replaces the zones: make a backup first.
USB connection
Tuning (receive only)
SSTV
Pick the USB device of your UV-K5 and tap “Query”. If it does not appear, check the OTG cable and try again.
Enter a frequency between 136 and 470 MHz and tap “Tune”. The tuning is renewed until STOP. Receive only.
Send a Robot36 image or record a reception. Sending transmits: check frequency and licence, and use the stop button to end it.
Forwards the radio’s USB port to another application. Use it only if you know which program will read it.
Control your Quansheng UV-K5 over USB. Connect first, then tune. Receive only on this screen.
Read, edit and save the Quansheng channels. Make a full backup before writing.
Decode SSTV images from a WAV file. No radio needed.
Receive Morse and Robot36 with the phone microphone. Receive only.
FT8 and digital modes with your radio. You need accurate time and your callsign; transmitting goes on the air.
Offline channel templates to export to your radio. Check local regulations.
Run a net: log participants and export the summary. Works offline.
CAT control of your radio over USB. Connect first, then use frequency, memories, digital or satellite. Sections that transmit say so.
Radtel RT-950 Pro over Bluetooth: connection, backup, APRS, messages and zones. Back up before writing.
Check cables, USB ports and your radio’s response. It does not transmit.
Shows your OpenGD77’s screen and sets its clock over USB. It does not transmit.
APRS chat through a KISS TNC over Bluetooth or network. Sending is transmitting.
Point your antenna with the BricoHams rotor over Bluetooth. Make sure the area is clear.
